prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 2015 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core approach: “Britain can be better” by making the economy work for working people. Budget Responsibility Lock: every policy is paid for with no extra borrowing; the deficit will be cut every year; current budget to surplus and debt falling as soon as possible; OBR auditing of manifestos.

Economy, tax and business
- Balance the books with fairer choices: restore 50p top rate; introduce a 10p starting rate; no rises in basic/higher Income Tax, NI or VAT; abolish non‑dom status; close loopholes; review HMRC culture.
- Pro‑business and pro‑worker strategy: most competitive G7 corporation tax, but cut and freeze business rates for 1.5m small firms; Small Business Administration; tackle late payment.
- British Investment Bank and regional banks; increase banking competition; levy on payday lenders to back credit unions.
- Infrastructure and productivity: National Infrastructure Commission; HS2 (control costs) and better northern rail; roads maintenance; cycling; swift decision on airport capacity; universal affordable high‑speed broadband and better mobile coverage.
- Green industrial strategy: legal 2030 decarbonised power target; empower Green Investment Bank; Energy Security Board; 1m additional green jobs.
- Corporate reform: strengthen long‑termism; curb excessive executive pay; employee voice on pay committees; tougher takeover rules; support co‑ops and mutuals; keep 30% Royal Mail in public hands with staff trust.

Work, skills and young people
- Raise National Minimum Wage to >£8 by Oct 2019; promote Living Wage via procurement and first‑year tax rebates; public companies to report on Living Wage.
- Ban exploitative zero‑hours (12‑week regular-hours right to a contract); end agency-worker undercutting; scrap employment tribunal fees system.
- Apprenticeship guarantee for qualified school leavers; require apprenticeships in large public contracts and for firms hiring skilled non‑EU workers; create Technical Degrees; gold‑standard, Level 3+ apprenticeships.
- Cut university tuition fees to £6,000; tackle unpaid internships.
- Compulsory Jobs Guarantee (youth 12+ months; over‑25s 24+ months), funded by a bank bonus tax.

Cost of living and markets
- Freeze energy bills to 2017, empower regulator to cut bills; break up Big Six generation/supply; simpler tariffs; protect SMEs; energy‑efficiency loans and warm homes.
- Water: national affordability scheme; stronger regulator.
- Transport: reform franchising; allow public operator; National Rail body; freeze fares next year and cap rises; cheapest-ticket right; city/county bus franchising and smart ticketing.

NHS, care and mental health
- Recruit 20,000 nurses, 8,000 GPs, 3,000 midwives funded by a Mansion Tax on £2m+ properties, tobacco levy, anti‑avoidance.
- 48‑hour GP appointments; one‑week cancer tests; Cancer Treatments Fund.
- Repeal Health and Social Care Act; NHS preferred provider; cap private profit; integrate physical, mental and social care with single care plans and coordinators; parity for mental health; talking therapies within 28 days.
- End 15‑minute care visits; hire 5,000 home‑care workers; support carers.

Education
- Protect entire education budget (early years to post‑16); cap infant classes at 30; all teachers qualified; Master Teacher path; College of Teaching; Directors of School Standards; end Free Schools programme; Technical Baccalaureate; Institutes of Technical Education; English and Maths to 18; stronger careers advice.

Families, housing and welfare
- Free childcare 25 hours/week for working parents of 3–4 year‑olds; guaranteed wraparound primary childcare (8am–6pm); double paternity leave to 4 weeks and raise pay.
- Build at least 200,000 homes/year by 2020; first dibs for local first‑time buyers; “use it or lose it” land powers; garden cities; three‑year private tenancies with rent rise ceiling; ban letting fees; landlord register; abolish Bedroom Tax.
- Keep overall benefit cap (review regional levels); no tax credit cuts; pause and review Universal Credit; new Youth Allowance linked to training; reform Work Capability Assessment; tailored disability employment support.

Immigration, safety and rights
- 1,000 extra border staff; full exit checks; two‑year wait for EU migrants’ benefits; English requirement for public‑facing staff; ban overseas‑only recruitment and worker exploitation; humane enforcement, end indefinite detention for vulnerable groups.
- Protect neighbourhood policing (safeguard 10,000 officers); scrap PCCs; Victims’ Law; Violence against Women and Girls Bill and commissioner; tougher hate‑crime laws; overhaul Prevent.
- Constitutional reform: people‑led Convention; replace House of Lords with elected Senate of the Nations and Regions; English Devolution Act (£30bn powers to regions); votes at 16; tougher lobbyist register; ban MPs’ paid directorships; gender pay gap reporting.

Europe and the world
- Remain in and reform the EU; complete single market; protect non‑Euro members; referendum lock on any power transfer.
- Defence Review; uphold NATO; retain Trident CASD while pursuing multilateral disarmament; strengthen veterans’ support and Military Covenant.
- Climate leadership: push for net‑zero global emissions in second half of century; flood prevention; air quality; end badger cull.
- International development: keep 0.7% aid; focus on poorest countries; Centre for Universal Health Coverage; tackle tax avoidance and corruption; human rights envoys (LGBT, Religious Freedom).
